candidates.creator: Spaceflightpedia
candidates.title: Apollo 11's Computer Overloaded During the Landing - Mission Control Said GO #shorts
candidates.description:
About seven minutes before touchdown, the Apollo 11 lunar module computer threw a 1202 alarm: it had more work than time. Twenty-six-year-old guidance officer Steve Bales, backed by Jack Garman and his handwritten alarm list, called GO. The overload came from the rendezvous radar, switched on in case of an abort, which flooded the computer with junk signals. The guidance computer had 2,048 words of erasable memory (about 4 KB) and 36,864 words of read-only memory.

Would you have said go, or abort? Tell us in the comments.

candidates.title: Unnamed Life, 4km Down, Under 1979 Scars #Shorts
candidates.description:
Four kilometres of water is close to half the height of Mount Everest, and all of it is resting on one small animal.

New deep-sea species discovered in 2026 are being photographed for minutes at a time in the Clarion-Clipperton Zone, a dark abyssal plain in the Pacific larger than India. This video follows a single beam of light into the black, where a 1979 test-mining track still scars the seabed and roughly 90% of the recorded animals have no scientific name yet. We look at the cold, the pressure, the nodules that grow millimetres per million years, and what is lost when the lights switch off.

Timestamps:
0:00 Hook

2:30 Where the Light Ends
4:30 The 1979 Furrow
7:00 The Names We Haven't Given

2021年2月18日、探査車パーサヴィアランスが火星に降りた7分間を、探査車のカメラが撮った本物の映像で降りていきます。この7分間、地球の技術者は映像を見ながら操縦していたのでしょうか、それとも何もできずに待っていたのでしょうか。降りながら撮った写真を、積んできた地図と見比べて居場所を出す「地形の照合」とスカイクレーンの仕組み、降りた場所の本物の3D、火星の風の音、青い夕焼けまで紹介します。

0:00 パラシュートが開く本物の映像

8:22 答え合わせ（11分22秒）
9:06 落ちた部品と、降りた場所の3D
10:42 湖を東京23区と比べる
11:01 初めての色付きの写真
11:27 火星の風の音
11:59 ヘリ、インジェニュイティ
13:31 火星の青い夕焼け
14:05 2027年2月、日本から火星を探す
15:24 次回予告

What does it take to cast your vote when you are 400 kilometres above Earth? As millions of Americans head to the polls for the crucial 2026 US midterm elections, NASA astronaut Anil Menon has taken part in the democratic process from an extraordinary location – the International Space Station.

Orbiting Earth aboard the ISS, Menon revealed that he completed an electronic ballot on his computer and transmitted it to election officials in Harris County, Texas. He also said that all three American crew members aboard the space station had the opportunity to exercise their right to vote.

Menon's vote highlights how American astronauts can participate in elections even while working hundreds of kilometres above the planet. The process allows eligible US citizens in space to remain part of the country's democratic system.

Back on Earth, the 2026 US midterm elections could dramatically reshape the balance of power in Washington. Democrats are eyeing control of the House of Representatives, while the battle for the Senate remains uncertain.

candidates.creator: Dusty Mammoth
candidates.title: NASA Couldn't Help. This Rover Had to Land Itself on Mars.
candidates.description:
aOn February 18, 2021, NASA's Perseverance rover hit the top of Mars's atmosphere at nearly 12,500 mph and had about seven minutes to come to a dead stop on the ground. With radio signals taking more than 11 minutes to reach Earth, nobody at mission control could step in.

Here's how it did it, step by step: a heat shield that reached about 2,370°F, a 70-foot supersonic parachute, a camera that matched the ground to a stored map and picked its own safe spot, eight rocket engines, and the sky crane that lowered the rover on cables about 21 feet long.

The onboard footage in this video is real: it was shot by Perseverance's own cameras during the landing.

Footage: NASA / JPL-Caltech (Perseverance descent and touchdown onboard camera views; Mars 2020 landing animations; JPL mission control)

- NASA Science, Perseverance entry, descent and landing (science.nasa.gov)
- NASA, "Perseverance Rover Decelerates in the Martian Atmosphere" (nasa.gov)
- Spaceflight Now, "Mars rover ready for riskiest part of $2.7 billion mission" (Feb. 17, 2021)

candidates.title: This 4-Pound Helicopter Flew on Mars. 72 Times.
candidates.description:
In 2021, a 4-pound helicopter named Ingenuity did something no aircraft had ever done: it flew on another planet. The air on Mars is about 1% as dense as Earth's, every command took minutes to arrive, and nights dropped to −130°F. NASA planned five test flights. It flew 72 times.

Key facts (NASA/JPL):
• First powered, controlled flight on another planet — April 19, 2021, Jezero Crater
• Rotors spin at roughly 2,400 rpm

candidates.title: How NASA Landed Perseverance Rover on Mars in 7 Minutes
candidates.description:
Nearly 20,000 km/h. A supersonic parachute. A rocket-powered sky crane. NASA’s Perseverance rover had around seven minutes to reach the surface of Mars.

On February 18, 2021, Perseverance landed in Jezero Crater after a descent that ended with the rover being lowered on three cables. Once its six wheels touched down, the cables were cut and the rocket stage flew away.

Its mission was only beginning. Jezero once held a lake, making it a promising place to search for signs of ancient microbial life. Perseverance studies the rocks, drills cores and seals samples for future analysis.

In 2025, scientists reported a potential biosignature in a rock called Cheyava Falls. Nonliving chemical processes could also explain the finding, so its origin remains under investigation.

By October 11, 2026, Perseverance had travelled 45.22 kilometres, breaking the record for driving on another world. NASA has approved continued exploration of Jezero’s rim through roughly the end of 2028.

This video uses AI-generated reconstructions based on NASA/JPL-Caltech imagery and mission information. Original NASA photographs are included where indicated. Mission information checked November 4, 2026.

Since a PS5 system update in September 2025, the DualSense and DualSense Edge can remember four devices instead of one, and the four shape buttons are the slots: triangle is slot one, circle is two, cross is three and square is four. To add a PC, Mac, phone, tablet or Apple TV, unplug any USB cable and turn the controller off, then hold the PS button and a shape button for about five seconds until the lights flash twice, and pair it from that device’s Bluetooth settings. Your PS5 doesn’t need the combo, because pairing the controller with the console the usual way puts it in the next open slot by itself. To switch, turn on the device you want and hold the same two buttons for about three seconds. It works whether the controller is on or off, and the lights under the touchpad show which slot you’ve landed on. Before this, playing on a PC meant pairing the controller all over again, then pairing it back to the console afterwards. If all four slots are in use, pairing a new device replaces whichever one you haven’t connected to for the longest.

candidates.description:
🔴 Perseverance Makes History on Mars
On February 18, 2021, NASA's Perseverance rover successfully achieved a historic, completely autonomous landing on the dusty surface of Mars. Touching down inside the ancient Jezero Crater, this cutting-edge mobile laboratory began its critical mission to hunt for signs of ancient microbial life and collect vital rock core samples.

🤖 Onboard Computers Handle the Ultimate Test
Because radio signals take over 11 minutes to travel the vast distance between Mars and Earth, real-time human control from mission control was completely impossible. Highly advanced onboard computers had to handle the entire landing sequence independently, guiding the spacecraft through atmospheric entry, parachute deployment, and the final rocket-powered sky crane maneuver.

🚀 Conquering the Seven Minutes of Terror
This intense, nerve-wracking descent phase is famously known by aerospace engineers as the "Seven Minutes of Terror." The flawless execution of this robotic landing perfectly demonstrates the incredible evolution of artificial intelligence and automated navigation systems required to pioneer the future of deep-space exploration.

candidates.title: A Rover Filmed Its Own Mars Landing 🪂
candidates.description:
This is real footage of NASA's Perseverance rover landing in Jezero Crater on Mars on February 18, 2021, recorded by its own entry, descent and landing cameras: cameras looking up at the parachute, one looking down from the descent stage, one on the rover looking up, and one on the rover's belly looking at the ground. The 70.5-foot (21.5-meter) supersonic parachute opened about 7 miles above the surface while the spacecraft was moving about 940 mph (1,512 km/h). After the heat shield fell away, the rocket-powered descent stage lowered the rover on cables about 21 feet (6.4 meters) long, the "sky crane" maneuver, then flew off to crash a safe distance away. The parachute's orange and white pattern spells JPL's motto, "Dare Mighty Things," in binary, one word per ring, with the GPS coordinates of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory around the outer edge. Radio signals took about 11 minutes to travel from Mars to Earth that day, so the rover had already landed by the time mission control heard the parachute had opened.

[지금 이 시간 가장 뜨거운 뉴스를 '콕' 찍어 전해드립니다]

도널드 트럼프 대통령에 대한 중간평가라고도 할 수 있는 미국 중간선거가 현지시간 3일 미 전역에서 치러졌는데요.

그런데, 특별한 곳에서도 소중한 한 표가 행사됐습니다.

▶ 인터뷰 : 아닐 메논 / NASA 소속 비행사
- "우주정거장에 오신 것을 환영합니다. 오늘 이곳에서 투표할 수 있는 특권을 누리게 됐습니다."

국제우주정거장, ISS에 체류 중인 미국 항공우주 NASA 소속 비행사 아닐 메논도 전자 투표를 마쳤습니다.

▶ 인터뷰 : 아닐 메논 / NASA 소속 비행사
- "여기가 제 방인데, 저에게는 투표소 역할도 하는 공간입니다."

임시 투표소로 변신한 곳은 다름 아닌 메논의 개인 침실이었습니다.

▶ 인터뷰 : 아닐 메논 / NASA 소속 비행사
"저는 방 안에 있는 컴퓨터로 전자투표용지를 작성해 해리스 카운티에 전송할 수 있었습니다. 그렇게 오늘 투표를 마쳤습니다."

메논을 비롯해 ISS에 체류 중인 NASA 소속 비행사 3명이 전자 투표를 마쳤습니다.

이들이 작성한 전자 투표용지는 여러 단계를 거쳐 지상으로 전달됩니다.

먼저 암호화된 상태로 NASA의 근지구 네트워크를 통해 뉴멕시코 지상 안테나로 전달됩니다.

이후 휴스턴 제어센터를 거쳐 텍사스주 해리스 카운티로 최종 전송되는 방식입니다.

한편, 트럼프 대통령의 남은 2년 임기의 운명을 가를 중간선거 결과는 한국시간으로 이르면 오늘 오후부터 윤곽이 드러날 것으로 예상됩니다.

일부 주에서는 이미 투표가 마감됐고, 순차적으로 개표가 진행됩니다.

현지에서는 트럼프 행정부에 대한 심판을 바라는 이른바 '앵그리 트럼프' 유권자들과, 

여론조사에선 드러나지 않다가 투표장에서 지지를 보내는 '샤이 트럼프'의 결집이 주요 변수가 될 것으로 보고 있습니다.

candidates.creator: Galactic Brief
candidates.title: On Mars, Sound Travels at Two Different Speeds 🔴
candidates.description:
On Mars, sound has two speed limits. Perseverance's microphones showed that in the thin, cold, carbon-dioxide air, low-pitched sounds travel at about 240 m/s while higher-pitched sounds travel at about 250 m/s. On Earth, sound moves at about 343 m/s, so Mars slows it by roughly 30%.

Mars is so quiet that the science team at one point thought the microphone was broken. High-pitched sounds fade quickly and are lost at about 26 feet (8 meters). Yet the rover still caught the faint, low hum of the Ingenuity helicopter's rotors from about 262 feet (80 meters) away.

Sources: NASA/JPL, "What Sounds Captured by NASA's Perseverance Rover Reveal About Mars"; Maurice et al., "In situ recording of Mars soundscape," Nature 605 (2022); NASA/JPL, "NASA's Perseverance Captures Video, Audio of Fourth Ingenuity Flight."

candidates.creator: 3D_Engineering
candidates.title: Why a One-Ton Rover Cuts Itself Loose | NASA's Sky Crane
candidates.description:
Why lower a one-ton rover on ropes, then cut it loose? Discover how NASA's Sky Crane delivered Curiosity to Mars using gravity-driven bridle deployment, a tapered spool, and an electrical descent brake. Gears drive a generator, and resistors turn the rover's deployment energy into heat. Once the ropes are fully extended, rockets control the final descent. After touchdown is confirmed, pyrotechnic cutters sever the connections so the descent stage can fly away, leaving the rover on the surface.

This video uses 3D engineering visualizations to explain the landing sequence.

David Dowen, Jeff Moser and Jeff Mobley / Sierra Nevada Corporation

candidates.creator: Epic Factx
candidates.title: NASA's Mars Lander Switched Off Its Own Engines
candidates.description:
On 3 December 1999, NASA's Mars Polar Lander went silent as planned for entry, and was never heard from again.

Investigators' most probable cause: while the lander hung from its parachute, its three legs snapped open. The jolt made a magnetic touchdown sensor flash a false "landed" signal. The software kept it. When touchdown sensing switched on about 40 metres above the surface, the computer cut the engines. The lander would have hit Mars at about 22 m/s instead of 2.4 m/s.

The wreck has never been confirmed. The crash shown is a 3D reconstruction of the most probable scenario, not real footage.

In 2008, Phoenix, built from the same 2001 test lander, landed safely on Mars' northern arctic plains.

NASA Astronaut Anil Menon Votes From Space Station in US Midterm Elections 2026 | hmtv

#nasa #astronaut #vote #uselection #hmtv 

అంతరిక్షం నుంచే ఓటేసిన అనిల్ మీనన్




STORY: Three NASA astronauts, including Anil Menon, on Tuesday cast their ballots in the US midterm elections from the International Space Station orbiting over 400 kms above Earth.

Menon and two other astronauts – Luke Delaney and Jessica Watkins – filled out an electronic ballot and sent it securely to election officials.

"Yes, you can even vote from space," Menon said in a post on X.

Menon reached the International Space Station on July 14 on board a Russian Soyuz mission. Delaney and Watkins reached the orbital laboratory on October 1 onboard a SpaceX rocket.

"All three US crew members had the privilege of voting from Space Station. We filled out an electronic ballot and sent it securely to the election officials," Menon said.

The US is voting in the midterm elections on Tuesday to elect 435 members of the House of Representatives, 37 members of the Senate, 36 state governors and a host of local elected officials.   Like most data transmitted between the space station and mission control, the ballot traverses through NASA’s Near Space Network, managed by the Goddard Space Flight Centre in Greenbelt, Maryland.

The ballot is encrypted and only accessible by the astronaut and the clerk to preserve the vote's integrity.

In a short video, Menon said he exercised his franchise inside his room on the ISS, which doubled up as a polling booth.

Menon said he filled out an electronic form and sent it to Harris County in Texas.

candidates.title: John Glenn Went Back to Space at 77, and He Was a Senator at the Time #shorts
candidates.description:
October 29, 1998: John Glenn, 77 years old and a sitting United States senator from Ohio, lifts off aboard the space shuttle Discovery on STS-95. In February 1962 he had been the first American to orbit the Earth, three times in under five hours, and the country gave him a parade with President Kennedy. Then NASA never flew him again; Glenn said he learned years later that Kennedy did not want to risk losing him. He left NASA in 1964 and served 24 years in the Senate. Starting in 1995 he lobbied NASA administrator Dan Goldin for a seat; Goldin wanted a scientific reason and a pass on the same physical the younger astronauts took. Glenn passed, and flew as a payload specialist so researchers could study sleep and the aging body in orbit. Discovery flew almost nine days and 3.6 million miles. Glenn's record as the oldest person in space stood 23 years, until Wally Funk flew at 82 in July 2021, and William Shatner at 90 that October.

Sources: Wikipedia, STS-95, John Glenn and Wally Funk; Ohio State University, Friendship 7 archive; NPR and CBS interviews with Glenn.

candidates.creator: Space Consult
candidates.title: Highlights Visit Astronaut Marsha Ivins at Apollo and Beyond
candidates.description:
To conclude our series of astronaut events this year, we welcomed NASA astronaut Marsha Ivins to the Technik Museum Speyer on October 23 and 24, 2026. Before a roughly two-and-a-half-hour tour of »Apollo and Beyond«, Europe’s largest exhibition of human spaceflight, Marsha Ivins signed the autograph board, which now features 76 astronauts and cosmonauts. Some of the highlights of the tour for Marsha were the documentation of her five Space Shuttle missions, the Soviet space shuttle »Buran OK-GLI« and the »The Moon« exhibition area, featuring a mockup of the Apollo 11 lunar module (LM-5) »Eagle«, as well as replicas of the Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV), the Apollo 17 A7LB spacesuits of CDR Gene Cernan and LMP Jack Schmitt, and the original lunar rock 15499.67, collected during the second extravehicular activity (EVA-2) at Station 4 at Dune Crater during the Apollo 15 mission. A special exhibit on the Space Shuttle platform was the original »Protein Crystallization Facility« (PCF), which spent about a year aboard the »EURECA« science platform. »EURECA« was launchehed into space during her second mission, STS-46, and deployed into Earth orbit. After the tour, Marsha Ivins was available to the media for interviews. Following that, space journalist and exhibition director Gerhard Daum conducted an extended interview with Marsha Ivins about her 36 years at NASA, including 26 years as an astronaut, her five Space Shuttle missions, as well as her visit to the »Apollo and Beyond« space exhibition.
The next day, Marsha Ivins gave a very engaging and humorous presentation at the museum’s FORUM on the 65-year history of U.S. human spaceflight. She also provided a glimpse into the future of commercial space stations following the ISS, as well as missions to the Moon and Mars. Her career highlights and her five Space Shuttle missions rounded out the presentation. Afterward, Gerhard Daum moderated a panel discussion with Marsha and a Q&A session with the audience. To wrap things up, children up to age 14 had the opportunity to have their picture taken with the astronaut. The children are always thrilled to have their parents take a souvenir photo of them with an astronaut. We are very pleased that once again, about 350 visitors attended the exciting lecture and were delighted by Marsha and our program.

Zum Abschluss unserer Astronautenveranstaltungen in diesem Jahr, konnten wir am 23. und 24. Oktober 2026 NASA-Astronautin Marsha Ivins im Technik Museum Speyer begrüßen. Vor einem etwa zweieinhalbstündigen Rundgang durch Europas größte Ausstellung der bemannten Raumfahrt »Apollo and Beyond« signierte Marsha Ivins die Autogrammtafel auf der nun 76 Astronautinnen und Astronauten sowie Kosmonauten vertreten sind. Einige Höhepunkte des Rundgangs waren für Marsha die Dokumentation Ihrer 5 Space Shuttle Missionen, die sowjetische Raumfähre »Buran OK-GLI« sowie der Ausstellungsbereich »Der Mond« mit einem Mockup der Apollo 11 Mondfähre (LM-5) »Eagle« sowie den Repliken des Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV), der Apollo 17 A7LB Spacesuits von CDR Gene Cernan und LMP Jack Schmitt sowie dem originalen Mondstein 15499,67, von der zweiten Exkursion (EVA-2) der Station 4 am Dune Crater der Apollo 15 Mission. Ein besonderes Exponat auf der Space Shuttle Plattform war das originale »Protein Crystalization Facility« (PCF) das etwa ein Jahr auf der Wissenschaftsplattform »EURECA« geflogen ist. »EURECA« wurde bei Ihrer zweiten Mission STS-46 in den Weltraum befördert und im Erdorbit ausgesetzt. Nach dem Rundgang stand Marsha Ivins den Medien für Interviews zur Verfügung. Im Anschluss führte Raumfahrtjournalist und Ausstellungsleiter Gerhard Daum mit Marsha Ivins ein längeres Interview über Ihre 36 Jahre bei der NASA, davon 26 Jahre als Astronautin, Ihre 5 Space Shuttle Missionen sowie Ihren Besuch der Raumfahrtausstellung »Apollo and Beyond«.
Am nächsten Tag hielt Marsha Ivins im FORUM des Museums einen sehr spannenden und humorvollen Vortrag über die 65-jährige Geschichte der bemannten Raumfahrt der USA. Sie gab auch einen Ausblick über die zukünftigen kommerziellen Raumstationen nach der ISS sowie Missionen zum Mond und Mars. Ihr Werdegang sowie Ihre 5 Space Shuttle Missionen rundeten den Vortrag ab. Im Anschluss moderierte Gerhard Daum eine Talkrunde mit Marsh und einer Q&A mit dem Publikum. Zum Abschluss konnten sich Kinder bis 14 Jahren mit der Astronautin fotografieren lassen. Die Kinder sind jedes Mal begeistert sich mit einer Astronautin oder einem Astronauten für ein Erinnerungsfoto von ihren Eltern fotografieren zu lassen. Wir freuen uns sehr das wieder etwa 350 Besucher bei dem spannenden Vortrag dabei waren und von Marsha und unserem Programm begeistert waren.

candidates.creator: AI: Beyond the Surface
candidates.title: How NASA Landed Curiosity on Mars: 7 Minutes of Terror | #space #curiosityrover #mars #nasa
candidates.description:
How do you land a car on Mars? NASA's Curiosity rover is about the size of a small SUV (NASA's wording) and weighs 899 kg. On 6 August 2012 (UTC) it landed in Gale Crater, near Mount Sharp, using entry, a parachute, rockets and a "sky crane", with no one on Earth able to steer it.

Entry: Curiosity's capsule hit the top of the Martian atmosphere at about 13,200 mph (5,900 m/s, NASA), about 21,000 km/h in our conversion. NASA predicted its heat shield would reach about 2,100 °C. An air-bag landing like the earlier rovers' was not an option for a rover this size and weight (NASA).

Parachute: a 16 m (51 ft) parachute opened faster than sound, about 11 km up (NASA press kit). NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter even photographed Curiosity hanging under it.

Why "7 minutes of terror": entry to touchdown took about seven minutes, but on landing day a radio signal took 13.8 minutes to cross from Mars to Earth. So Curiosity was already on the ground about 6½ minutes before Earth even heard it had entered the atmosphere (our calculation from JPL's event times). The computer had to fly the whole landing by itself. NASA's 2012 video says the landing "is referred to as the '7 minutes of terror'".

The answer, the sky crane: with the heat shield and backshell gone, the descent stage fired its eight rocket engines. About 20 m up, the sky crane lowered Curiosity on three nylon cords, about 7.5 m long, at a constant 0.75 m/s (2.7 km/h, walking pace, our conversion). The rover's wheels doubled as landing gear. When it sensed touchdown, the cords were cut and the descent stage flew off and crashed about 650 m away, on purpose, well clear of the rover and its landing site (NASA / HiRISE). NASA reused the same sky crane for Perseverance in 2021, and Curiosity is still exploring Mars 14 years later.

Would you trust the computer to land it alone, or would you build a smaller rover that can bounce down on airbags? Tell me below.

Sources:
NASA/JPL — Mars Science Laboratory Landing Press Kit (July 2012): https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/press_kits/MSLLanding.pdf
NASA — Challenges of Getting to Mars: Curiosity's Seven Minutes of Terror (22 June 2012): https://science.nasa.gov/resource/challenges-of-getting-to-mars-curiositys-seven-minutes-of-terror/
NASA — How We Land on Mars: https://science.nasa.gov/planetary-science/programs/mars-exploration/mission-timeline/how-we-land-on-mars/
NASA JPL — Timeline of major mission events during Curiosity's landing: https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/timeline-of-major-mission-events-during-curiositys-landing/
NASA — Mars Science Laboratory: Curiosity rover ("about the size of a small SUV"): https://science.nasa.gov/mission/msl-curiosity/
NASA Photojournal — PIA15978, Curiosity under its parachute (HiRISE): https://photojournal.jpl.nasa.gov/catalog/PIA15978
NASA Photojournal — PIA15696, rover, heat shield, backshell and sky-crane impact site: https://photojournal.jpl.nasa.gov/catalog/PIA15696
University of Arizona HiRISE — ESP_028678_1755 (descent stage crash site): https://www.uahirise.org/ESP_028678_1755
NASA — Curiosity mission updates: https://science.nasa.gov/mission/msl-curiosity/science-updates/
NASA PDS Geosciences — MGS MOLA elevation data (MEGDR, 64 px/degree): https://pds-geosciences.wustl.edu/mgs/mgs-m-mola-5-megdr-l3-v1/mgsl_300x/meg064/

Images: real photo of Curiosity under its parachute, seen from orbit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/Univ. of Arizona (PIA15978). Ground detail near the landing site: HiRISE, NASA/JPL-Caltech/Univ. of Arizona (from PIA15696). Terrain relief: NASA Mars Global Surveyor MOLA elevation data.
3D visuals are illustrations: the rover, descent stage, capsule, parachute, plasma, plumes and dust are our models; terrain relief follows NASA MOLA data around Gale Crater with illustrative colours. The sky-crane opening shot is a slowed flash-forward. The speed gauge uses NASA's key figures (km/h is our conversion); values between those points are illustrative. Narration is an AI voice.

candidates.title: New Deep-Sea Species, and a 1979 Scar That Never Healed
candidates.description:
New deep-sea species discovered in 2026 are being photographed for minutes at a time in the Clarion-Clipperton Zone, a dark abyssal plain in the Pacific larger than India. This video follows a single beam of light into the black, where a 1979 test-mining track still scars the seabed and roughly 90% of the recorded animals have no scientific name yet. We look at the cold, the pressure, the nodules that grow millimetres per million years, and what is lost when the lights switch off.

Timestamps:
0:00 Hook
1:00 The Weight of the Water
2:30 Where the Light Ends
4:30 The 1979 Furrow
7:00 The Names We Haven't Given
8:30 What Changes Now

This is a mystery-first look at the deep ocean. We are not here to deliver a verdict. We are here to hold the dark a little longer, because the unknown is far larger than the known.

#DeepSea #Ocean #DeepSeaDiscovery #ClarionClipperton #Mystery
